skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray with a suspected mediastinal mass to determine its specific anatomical compartment and laterality.
steps: Inspect the upper mediastinum and paratracheal regions for asymmetrical soft-tissue widening or bulging contours.
Identify the side of the mass by observing which paratracheal stripe is obliterated or expanded (e.g., right vs. left upper mediastinum).
Distinguish from bilateral hilar adenopathy by confirming the opacity is located in the superior mediastinum/paratracheal area rather than primarily at the lung hila.

skills.trigger: When assessing the severity and mass effect of a mediastinal lesion on adjacent airway structures.
steps: Trace the course of the tracheal air column from the thoracic inlet downwards.
Check for deviation of the trachea away from the side of the mass, indicating a space-occupying lesion exerting pressure.
Differentiate 'displacement' (trachea pushed to the contralateral side) from 'central compression' (narrowing without significant lateral shift) or 'no effect' (midline trachea).
